title: Noah and the Rainbow
bigQuestion: What does the story of Noah say about a big flood and a promise?

story.title: Rain on the Window
story.kicker: It rains all day, and a picture book shows a boat full of animals.
paragraphs: Rain taps on the window. Leo cannot go outside. He pulls a picture book off the shelf. On the cover is a big wooden boat. Animals look out of the windows. Two giraffes. Two lions. Two ducks.
"That is Noah's boat," says his dad. "The story is in Genesis, in the Bible. It says a flood was coming. So Noah built a very big boat. He put his family and the animals inside."
Leo turns the pages. Rain falls on the boat for forty days. Then a bird flies out. It comes back with a green leaf. Leo points at the last page. A rainbow stretches over the boat.
"The story says the rainbow was a promise," his dad says. Leo looks out the window. The rain is stopping. He waits to see if a rainbow will come.
story.think: What is a promise someone made to you? How did you know they would keep it?

lessons.title: Noah Builds a Boat
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God told Noah to build a big boat because a flood was coming.
reading: Genesis tells about a man named *Noah*. The story says people had become very unkind. God was sad about it. God told Noah a *flood* was coming.
God told Noah to build a boat. It was very big. It had three floors and one door. The story says Noah did just what he was told.
The boat in the story is called an *ark*. Noah built it out of wood. He covered it inside and out so water could not get in.

words.d: the man in the Genesis story who builds the big boat
a lot of water that covers the land
the very big boat in the story of Noah

look.title: How Big Was the Boat?
look.prompt: Which is the biggest number? Is the boat longer or taller?

check.q: Who built the boat in the story?
check.why: Genesis 6 says Noah built the ark.

check.q: Why did Noah build the boat in the story?
check.why: The story says God told Noah a flood was coming.

check.q: What is the big boat called?
check.why: The boat in the Noah story is called an ark.

lessons.title: Two of Each Animal
lessons.mainIdea: The story says animals came two by two, and then it rained for forty days.
reading: The story says the animals came to the boat. Two of each kind. A boy animal and a girl animal. Birds too. They all went in through the door.
Noah's family went in too. His wife, his three sons and their wives. Then the story says the door was shut.
Then the rain came. It rained for *forty* days and forty nights. Water covered the land. The boat floated on top.

words.d: the number 40; the story says it rained for forty days

look.title: Picture the Line of Animals
look.text: Look at a long line walking to a wooden boat. Two elephants. Two rabbits. Two snakes. Two owls. The line goes up a ramp and through one big door. Inside it is loud and warm.
look.prompt: What two animals would you want to see first in the line? What sounds would you hear?

check.q: How many of each kind of animal went in the boat?
check.why: The story says the animals came two by two.

check.q: How long did it rain in the story?
check.why: Genesis 7 says the rain fell forty days and forty nights.

check.q: Who went in the boat with the animals?
check.why: The story says Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives went in.

lessons.title: The Raven and the Dove
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Noah sent out birds to find out if the water was gone.
reading: The rain stopped. The boat came to rest on a mountain. But water was still everywhere. Noah wanted to know if the land was dry.
The story says Noah sent out a *raven*. It flew back and forth. Then Noah sent out a *dove*. The dove found no place to land. It came back.
Noah waited seven days. He sent the dove again. This time it came back with an *olive leaf* in its beak. Now Noah knew the water was going down.

words.d: a big black bird; the first bird Noah sent out in the story
a small gray or white bird; it brought back a leaf in the story
a small green leaf from an olive tree; a sign that land was dry

look.title: The Dove Comes Back
look.text: The story says the dove came back to Noah in the evening. In its mouth was an olive leaf it had picked. So Noah knew the water was going down from the earth.
look.cite: Genesis 8:11, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why did a leaf tell Noah the water was going down?

check.q: Which bird did Noah send out first in the story?
check.why: Genesis 8 says Noah sent out a raven first.

check.q: What did the dove bring back?
check.why: The story says the dove came back with an olive leaf.

check.q: What did the leaf tell Noah?
check.why: A leaf meant a tree was above the water, so the land was drying.

lessons.title: The Rainbow Promise
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the rainbow is a sign of a promise never to flood the whole earth again.
reading: At last the land was dry. The story says everyone came out of the boat. The animals ran off. Noah's family stepped onto the ground.
Then the story says God made a *promise*. Never again would a flood cover the whole earth. God put a *rainbow* in the clouds as a sign.
A promise is something you say you will do. Then you do it. In the story, the rainbow helps everyone remember the promise.

words.d: words that say you will do something, and then you do it
a bow of colors in the sky after rain; a sign of the promise in the story

look.title: A Bow in the Clouds
look.text: The story says God set a bow in the cloud. It would be a sign of the promise between God and the earth.
look.cite: Genesis 9:13, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What is something you use to help you remember a promise?

check.q: What was the rainbow a sign of in the story?
check.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow is the sign of God's promise.

check.q: What was the promise in the story?
choices: A flood would never cover the whole earth again
check.why: The story says God promised never to flood the whole earth again.

choices: Words that say you will do something, and then you do it
check.why: A promise is saying you will do something and then doing it.

lessons.title: The Tall Tower
lessons.mainIdea: The story of Babel says people built a tall tower and then began to speak many languages.
reading: Genesis has one more story after the flood. It says all people spoke one *language*. They said the same words. They understood each other.
The people wanted to build a *tower* up to the sky. The story says God saw the tower. God mixed up their words. Now they could not understand each other.
The people stopped building. They spread out over the earth. The place is called *Babel*. The story says this is why people speak many languages.

words.d: the words a group of people use to talk, like English or Spanish
the place in the story where the tall tower was built

look.title: A Tower Half Built
look.text: Look at a tower of bricks reaching up into the clouds. Workers stand on it. One shouts for a brick. The other hears words he does not know. He shrugs. They both put down their tools.
look.prompt: What do you do when someone talks in words you do not understand?

check.q: What did the people build in the story?
check.why: Genesis 11 says the people built a tower at Babel.

check.q: What happened to their words in the story?
check.why: The story says God mixed up their language so they could not understand each other.

check.q: What does the story say this explains?
check.why: The Babel story tells why people speak many languages.

lessons.title: Noah in Other Books
lessons.mainIdea: Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell a story of Noah, each in their own book.
reading: Jewish people read the story of Noah in the Torah. Christians read the same story in the Bible. It is the same book of Genesis.
Muslims tell a story of Noah too. In their holy book, the *Qur'an*, he is called *Nuh*. The Qur'an says Nuh warned people and built a boat.
The stories are alike in many ways. They are different in some ways too. Three groups of people tell about one man and one boat.

words.d: the name for Noah in the Qur'an

look.title: One Man, Three Books
look.text: In Genesis, Noah builds a boat, the rain comes, and a rainbow ends the story. In the Qur'an, Nuh warns his people for a long time, builds a boat, and the flood comes. Both tell of a boat and a flood. Only Genesis tells of the rainbow.
look.prompt: Name one thing the two stories share and one thing that is only in Genesis.

check.q: What is Noah called in the Qur'an?
check.why: In the Qur'an, Noah is called Nuh.

check.q: Who tells a story of Noah?
check.why: All three groups tell a story about Noah and a boat.
The Qur'an is the holy book of Muslims.

review.q: Why did Noah build the ark in the story?
review.why: The story says God told Noah a flood was coming.

review.q: How many of each animal went in the boat?
review.why: The story says the animals came two by two.

review.q: Which bird brought back an olive leaf?
review.why: Genesis 8 says the dove came back with an olive leaf.

review.q: What was the rainbow in the story?
review.why: The story says the rainbow was the sign of God's promise.

review.q: What happened at the tower of Babel?
choices: People began to speak many languages
review.why: The Babel story says people's words got mixed up into many languages.

review.q: Where do Muslims read about Nuh?
review.why: The Qur'an tells the story of Nuh, the name it gives Noah.
